html:
The publicly funded health service of the United Kingdom, launched on 5 July 1948. It offered care to everyone, free at the point of use and paid for mainly from taxes.

Before it, many people paid doctors directly or through insurance schemes that covered workers but often not their wives and children, and hospitals were a patchwork of charity and local council ones. The wartime Beveridge Report of 1942 called for a welfare state to fight "want, disease, ignorance, squalor and idleness".

Clement Attlee's Labour government, elected in 1945, carried it out. The Health Minister, Aneurin Bevan, a former coal miner from Wales, faced fierce resistance from doctors and won them over partly by letting them keep private patients. Hospitals were taken into public ownership.

The NHS became a pillar of the post war welfare state and one of Britain's most loved institutions. England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland now run separate services. Debates over its cost, waiting times and funding have run through British politics ever since.
sum: The publicly funded health service of the United Kingdom, launched on 5 July 1948. It offered care to everyone, free at the point of use and paid for mainly from taxes.
